concerns.text: Task T007 commits to generating a 'substantial set' of synthetic documents, whereas FR-001 and US-01 explicitly mandate '200 synthetic long documents'. This semantic weakening of the sample size requirement violates the fixed constraint needed for statistical power (SC-001, SC-004) and constitutes a requirement drift.

Task T011 explicitly instructs the code to NOT enforce or assert the '≥ 5%' threshold mentioned in US-01 Acceptance Scenario 1. While the code should not hard-code the hypothesis as a pass/fail gate, the task description fails to include a verification step to *measure and report* whether this threshold is met, effectively dropping the acceptance criterion from the implementation scope.

Task T019 (executing the retrieval pipeline) does not explicitly include the step to measure and report the 'false-positive rate' defined in SC-003 (retrieved snippet similarity < 0.5 AND no ground truth). While T017 mentions precision/recall, SC-003 defines a specific false-positive metric that is not covered by the task description, leaving this success criterion unverified.

Task T026 implements a hard-coded classification rule ('inverse' if r < -0.3) but omits the requirement from SC-002 to measure the coefficient against the 'null hypothesis of zero correlation' and report the specific p-value. The task conflates the classification logic with the statistical test output, risking the omission of the formal hypothesis test results required by the spec.

FR-008 requires measuring retrieval precision and recall 'against the ground-truth answers'. Tasks T016 and T017 describe generating queries and scoring similarity but fail to define the 'ground truth retrieval set' (i.e., which specific page/snippet *should* have been retrieved for each question) necessary to calculate False Positives/Negatives. This omission makes the FR-008 metric uncomputable as described.

Task T007b verifies the existence and checksum of PDFs but lacks a verification step to ensure the documents actually contain a valid 'middle-third' region with sufficient text density. This is a prerequisite for SC-001 (measuring accuracy recovery) and represents a dropped acceptance criterion for data validity.
